text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs presented Hungary's official application for NATO membership at the headquarters of the military alliance in Brussels on Wednesday.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn arrived in Singapore yesterday for a three-day official visit to promote bilateral ties.
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze pledged yesterday to bolster the police force with 1,800 new members as of July 1.

- Parliament's human rights committee yesterday recommended that Parliament make a political statement to dissociate itself from the anti-Semitic remark made in the House by Smallholder vice-president and Deputy Speaker Agnes Nagy Maczo.
- Hungary's trade deficit for the first two months came to HUF 71 billion or $431 million, the Central Statistical Office reports.
- The directors of the State Privatisation & Holding Co. decided to offer a 12.5 percent stake in the oil and gas company MOL to foreign institutional investors.

- The US human rights watchdog Freedom House says in its latest survey of Central and Eastern Europe that Hungary and the Czech Republic lead the region in compliance with political, economic and civil rights.
- An illegal slaughterhouse ignoring the most basic hygienic requirements was discovered near Debrecen early this week.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze and his Austrian counterpart Karl Schlogl are expected to sign an agreement in Vienna today extending the visa waiver, to permit visits of up to 90 days without a visa requirement.
- Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov will probably visit Budapest in July.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Industry and the Finance Ministry have proposed establishing a venture capital company owned by the Hungarian Development Bank, Eximbank, the Hungarian Foundation for Enterprise Promotion, the National Technical Development Committee and the Industry Ministry to enhance Hungarian investments in neighbouring countries.
- The Democratic Forum expects to sign a co-operation agreement with the Young Democrats after the latter's weekend congress, said party president Sandor Lezsak.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- Hungary and the Czech Republic have made the most thorough preparation for EU membership among the countries wishing to join the Union, according to the EU committee working out the terms of the accession agreements.

- The monthly devaluation rate of the forint may be reduced to 1 percent in the second half year, according to analyst Douglas Reid of ING Baring, adding inflation may fall to 16 percent, this paper quotes Reuters.
- Magyar Hitel Bank's pre-tax profit for 1996 was HUF 3.9 billion, some HUF 1.85 billion less than in the February preliminary report, the general meeting was informed yesterday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Hungarian Development Bank, Konzumbank's principal owner, stepped up preparations to merge Konzumbank with Corvinbank.
- The small Rakoczi Bank Rt increased its after-tax profit by 40 percent last year.
- Swedish Gripen fighter jets, American F-16 and F/A-18 Hornets and French Mirages will display their skills in Kecskemet May 24-25.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
